title: DeadDrop unknown privacy values fail-open to public
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: security

Spec 18.9 / LCI UI: privacy toggles are Public, OSCORE-Paired Only, Group Only. Private/group drops require a matching bound OSCORE context or 4.03; public listing must omit them.

render_post (deaddrop.py ~523-525):
  privacy = _senml_text(records, "privacy") or "public"
  if privacy not in {"public", "private", "group"}:
      privacy = "public"

Unknown or non-canonical values become public. add_drop is slightly different (unknown keeps the caller default) but the CoAP path is fail-open.

Evidence: POST pack() of n=privacy vs="Private" or vs="oscore-paired" or vs="restricted" stores privacy="public". Unauthenticated GET /deaddrop includes the payload; GET /deaddrop/{id} returns 2.05 and the body instead of 4.03.

Impact: a typo or a client using the UI label instead of the token publishes a drop that the sender marked as restricted. Confidentiality failure, not just a parse nit.

Oracle: spec 18.9 private/group -> 4.03 / omitted from public GET. Unknown MUST NOT fail-open.
acceptance_criteria: POST with privacy vs other than public/private/group (including Private, empty, and unknown tokens) must not list the drop on unauthenticated GET and must not return the body on unauthenticated GET /deaddrop/{id}. Prefer 4.00, or fail-closed as private. Canonical lowercase public/private/group keep current visibility.
